chunks: And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and al-Razzaz, from Ayyub ibn Nuh and Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sam'a, all of them from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from whoever narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding a man who divorced his wife while he was ill, he said: 'If he died during his illness and she had not married, she inherited him; and if she had already married, she has accepted what he did, so there is no inheritance for her.'
ai.seo_question: Does a wife inherit if her husband dies of illness after divorcing her before consummation or during the waiting period?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal status of a 'deathbed divorce' (talaq al-marad), establishing that the wife retains inheritance rights if she remains unmarried at the time of the husband's death, as the divorce is considered final. However, if she remarries, her subsequent marriage serves as definitive acceptance (rida) of the divorce, thereby forfeiting her share of the estate. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that the timing of death relative to the waiting period (iddah) and the wife's marital status determines the finality of the divorce for inheritance purposes.
